title: RFI - FEMA - Supply Chain Management System (SCMS)
description: FEMA�s Logistics Management Directorate, Logistics Systems Division, is conducting market research to identify commercially available cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions and associated services to transition, implement, operate, maintain, modernize, and support the FEMA Supply Chain Management System (SCMS). The anticipated requirement supports disaster logistics operations, including order and inventory management; warehouse and transportation operations; asset and in-transit visibility; point-of-distribution support; supply-chain reporting; procurement and enterprise resource planning interfaces; and financial reconciliation. FEMA is seeking solutions capable of supporting routine operations and scalable disaster-response surge requirements. The anticipated scope may include transition and implementation services, configuration and integration, recurring SaaS licensing, operations and maintenance, help desk and technical support, cybersecurity and system authorization support, continuity of operations, training, reporting, and optional surge capacity. FEMA anticipates a cloud-based solution or service model with approved system-to-system interfaces and applicable security, privacy, accessibility, and safeguarding requirements. This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government. No contract will be awarded from this RFI. Interested parties should review the attached Draft Statement of Work, Vendor Streamlined Profile Matrix, and Targeted Market Research Questionnaire for complete information and response instructions.

title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Open house Arzneimittelrabattverträge Nilotinib, ATC L01EA03 (ausgeschlossen Nilotinib dispergiert in Apfelmus, es sei denn, der Hersteller genießt hierfür Patentschutz)
description: Es handelt sich nicht um ein offenes Verfahren, sondern um ein sog. open-house-Modell! Das Formular für das offene Verfahren wird lediglich deshalb verwandt, da kein Formular für das open-house-Modell existiert. Verträge, die im open-house-Modell geschlossen werden, unterfallen mangels Auswahlentscheidung nicht dem Vergaberecht. Eine Unterwerfung unter vergaberechtliche Regelungen ist mit der Verwendung dieses Formulars nicht verbunden. Die AOK Bayern beabsichtigt, mit allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen nicht-exklusive Rabattvereinbarungen über den Wirkstoff Nilotinib, ATC L01EA03 (ausgeschlossen Nilotinib dispergiert in Apfelmus, es sei denn, der Hersteller genießt hierfür Patentschutz), nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zu schließen. Die AOK Bayern bietet allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, die die unten genannten Eignungsvoraussetzungen erfüllen, den Abschluss identischer und nicht individuell verhandelbarer Rabattvereinbarungen an. Der frühestmögliche Vertragsbeginn ist der 01.03.2025, alle Verträge enden am 28.02.2027. Ein Vertragsschluss ist während dieser Laufzeit jederzeit möglich, spätestens jedoch am 05.01.2027. Die Verträge können mit einer Frist von einem Monat zum Monatsende gekündigt werden. Bei Inkrafttreten eines durch bundesweite oder landesspezifische, im offenen Verfahren geschlossenen Rabattvertrags über Arzneimittel mit dem auftragsgegenständlichen Wirkstoff treten die open-house-Vereinbarungen automatisch für die entsprechende Laufzeit außer Kraft. Ein Vertrag wird mit allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen geschlossen, die ihre Eignung durch eine ausgefüllte und unterschriebene Eigenerklärung zur Zuverlässigkeit nachweisen. Der pharmazeutische Unternehmer hat den ausgefüllten und unterzeichneten (die Vertretungsberechtigung des/der Unterzeichner/s muss sich aus dem Handelsregisterauszug ergeben, anderenfalls ist eine Vollmacht vorzulegen) Vertrag nebst ausgefüllter und unterzeichneter Anlage "Festlegung der vertragsgegenständlichen Arzneimittel" sowie die ausgefüllte und unterzeichnete Eigenerklärung zur Zuverlässigkeit einzureichen. Die Unterlagen können ENTWEDER in SCHRIFTFORM von Hand unterzeichnet ODER ELEKTRONISCH mit einer qualifizierten elektronischen Signatur eingereicht werden. Von Hand unterzeichnete Unterlagen in SCHRIFTFORM sind in 2-facher Fassung im Original an folgende Adresse einzusenden: AOK Bayern - Die Gesundheitskasse Vergabestelle SGB V ZE25 open-house Rabattverträge Carl-Wery-Str. 28 81739 München ELEKTRONISCHE Unterlagen mit einer qualifizierten elektronischen Signatur sind über den Kommunikationsbereich im Vergabeportal www.dtvp.de einzureichen. Bei Eingang vollständiger und korrekter Unterlagen bis zum 05. eines jeden Monats erfolgt der Vertragsbeginn zum darauf folgenden nächsten Monatsersten, ansonsten zum darauf folgenden übernächsten Monatsersten. Bei von Hand unterzeichneten Unterlagen in SCHRIFTFORM ist eine Übersendung der vollständigen, ausgefüllten und unterzeichneten Unterlagen vorab per Fax (089/62730650151), als Scan an die E-Mail-Adresse vergabestelle1@by.aok.de oder über den Kommunikationsbereich im Vergabeportal www.dtvp.de fristwahrend, wenn die vollständigen und korrekten Originalunterlagen in Papierform bis zum 10. des Monats bei der AOK Bayern, Vergabestelle, eingehen. Bitte beachten Sie die Ausfüllanleitung, die unter www.dtvp.de bei den Vergabeunterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt wird. Interessierte pharmazeutische Unternehmen können im Projektraum zum Open-House-Verfahren auf dem Portal www.dtvp.de die Freischaltung der Vergabeunterlagen beantragen. Ein Link zum Portal befindet sich in dieser Bekanntmachung. Als potentielle Vertragspartner kommen ausschließlich pharmazeutische Unternehmen in Betracht. Die Unterlagen des Open-House-Verfahrens werden ausschließlich pharmazeutischen Unternehmen als potentiellen Vertragspartnern freigeschalten und sind streng vertraulich zu behandeln. Durch die Beantragung der Freischaltung durch die Unternehmen wird die vertrauliche Behandlung der Unterlagen bestätigt.

SOLE-SOURCE JUSTIFICATION The Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source: The Boeing Company (CAGE: 0B0D7), located in Layton, UT, under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1 (Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements). Market research, including a Sources Sought Synopsis (FA8214-25S-FT3PD) and Pre-solicitation Notice (FA821426RB004-PRESOL), concluded that Boeing is the only source with the unique technical data, specialized engineering expertise, and established manufacturing infrastructure required to meet the Government's strict performance schedules. Award to any other source would result in an estimated minimum duplication of $80M in costs and an unacceptable delay of at least three (3) years. 3. PROGRAM SCOPE & REQUIREMENTS The resulting contract is anticipated to be a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) vehicle containing the following primary parameters: Quantity: Production and delivery of twenty-five (25) FT3 flight test kits. Delivery Schedule: Just-in-time delivery to Vandenberg Space Force Base, CA, precisely 120 days prior to scheduled Operational Test Launches (OTLs). Period of Performance: October 2027 through September 2035. Total Estimated Program Value: Approximately $955M (including potential future procurements executed under an approved Class J&A). 4. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS & INTEREST This notice is not a request for competitive proposals, and a written solicitation will be issued directly to The Boeing Company. However, any responsible source that believes it can meet these requirements may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Information received will be evaluated solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responses must be submitted electronically to the Points of Contact listed below no later than the Response Deadline indicated in this posting.

title: France – Beach cleaning services – ENTRETIEN DES PLAGES ET DU LITTORAL
description: ***Le présent marché a pour objet, l'entretien des plages et du littoral de la commune de Roquebrune-sur-Argens et leur maintien en parfait état de propreté. Toutes les prestations du présent marché pourront être commandées à tout moment. L'entreprise devra mettre en oeuvre tous les moyens nécessaires à la réalisation des prestations suivantes : - Nettoiement des plages et du littoral : Cette opération comprend le nettoiement manuel des plages (de sables ou de galets), des criques, des ouvrages piétonniers divers (chemin des douanier, sentier, accès, mises à l'eau et autres cheminements), des grèves rocheuses, des ouvrages de protection des plages (talus, épis, sorties pluviaux...), ainsi que l'ensemble des secteurs se rattachant au périmètre défini au CCTP entre les limites de communes de Fréjus et Sainte Maxime. - Collecte des poubelles de plages et du littoral : Cette opération consiste à collecter les poubelles mises en place sur les plages, le long de la RD559 et du littoral Sambracitain (côté mer). - Le criblage des plages de sable : Cette opération comprend le nettoiement mécanique des plages de sable et des criques de sable se rattachant au périmètre défini à l'article 1.3.1. du CCTP. Cette prestation inclut la collecte et l'évacuation en décharge de tous déchets, détritus ou autres matières. - Le reprofilage ponctuel des plages et de leur accès à effectuer avant la période estivale et après les coups de mer ou fortes pluies (sorties de ruisseaux et pluviaux). - Gestion de la posidonie : Cette opération est à effectuer avant la période estivale et selon les besoins. En accord avec les préconisations environnementales, la posidonie sera déplacée sur la même plage, et stockée, par couches alternées posidonie/sable. - Gestion du volume de sable : Cette opération est à prévoir en amont de la saison et en fin de saison, le principe étant de constituer une réserve de sable en fin de saison qui permettra lors de la saison suivante " d'engraisser " les plages concernées. - Concassage des plages : Cette opération sera planifiée en amont de chaque saison en fonction des nécessités, afin d'améliorer la granulométrie du sable.

description: Předmětem zakázky je rekonstrukce mimoúrovňové křižovatky MÚK Držovice na silnici D46 (E462), která v současném stavu nevyhovuje platným technickým normám ani požadavkům na bezpečný a plynulý provoz. Součástí je také vybudování nové okružní křižovatky na ulici Konečná. Cílem zakázky je zvýšení bezpečnosti silničního provozu, zlepšení plynulosti dopravy a zajištění dlouhodobě vyhovujícího technického stavu dopravní infrastruktury na silnici D46.

title: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) Data Center, National Capital Region
description: Advance Procurement Notice   Data Center, (Modify design Built) National Capital Region (with Security Requirements) Purpose of this Advance Procurement Notice This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform design-builders of an upcoming contract opportunity located within the National Capital Region (Ontario). The purpose of this APN is to allow design-builders to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process, notably by initiating any necessary steps. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested design-builders to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). Description of the Project and Services It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed Project Number: WA257004 Contract Number: 88262 Title: Data Center NCR Approximate Estimate: 1.5B to 1.85B Anticipated Posting: Winter 2027 Description: To increase its capacity in supporting the mid to long-term objectives related to operations, security, and technology modernization, the Government of Canada is planning to design and construction a data center facility within the National Capital Region. This Data center of 60 MW will enable the onboarding of next-generation capabilities with tailored mechanical and electrical configurations to meet distinct technology requirements throughout the facility. The proposed data centre facility will also include a small office space and a shipping and receiving area. The estimated cost of the proposed Modified Design-Build (MDB) Contract exceeds $1.5 to 1.85B. It is anticipated that this solicitation will be initiated in Winter 2027.  This is conditional on receiving approval to proceed by the Government of Canada. Contract Award and Anticipated Security Requirements To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. As of the date of posting of this Advance Procurement Notice, the required security clearance(s) are anticipated to be: for design-builders: a valid Facility Security Clearance (FSC).  Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing design-builders early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, design-builders that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, design-builders are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the design-builders to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a design-builders has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Design-Builder that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca   Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Stephanie Tanguay Regional service line leader, Contract services Defence Construction Canada 613-715-4626 stephanie.tanguay@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process and does not provide any representations or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

description: Předmětem zakázky je rekonstrukce mimoúrovňové křižovatky MÚK Držovice na silnici D46 (E462), která v současném stavu nevyhovuje platným technickým normám ani požadavkům na bezpečný a plynulý provoz. Stávající mostní objekt ev. č. 46–014B je ve zhoršeném technickém stavu a vyžaduje nahrazení novou konstrukcí. Současně je nevyhovující uspořádání křižovatky z hlediska kapacity a bezpečnosti provozu. Realizací stavby dojde k přestavbě křižovatky, doplnění připojovacích a odbočovacích pruhů a úpravě dopravního řešení včetně napojení na okolní komunikační síť. Součástí je také vybudování nové okružní křižovatky na ulici Konečná. Cílem zakázky je zvýšení bezpečnosti silničního provozu, zlepšení plynulosti dopravy a zajištění dlouhodobě vyhovujícího technického stavu dopravní infrastruktury na silnici D46.

title: France-Villeneuve-Loubet: Motor vehicles
Mountainbike-Trails am Horneggli, Gemeinde Saanen
description:
• Realisierung von mehreren Mountainbike-Trails, die grösstenteils neu gebaut werden sollen. Einige kurze Abschnitte führen über bestehende Wege/Flurstrassen in Koexistenz mit anderen Nutzungsformen, teilweise mit Wandern oder teilweise mit der Landwirtschaft. Auf diesen müssen bikespezifische Unterhaltsmassnahmen (v.a. nachhaltiges Wasser-Entwässerung, Sicherung der Wegoberfläche) umgesetzt werden.
  • Die Strecken führen von den Bergstationen Horneggli, resp. Hornberg hinunter nach Schönried (Talstation Horneggli)
  • Ziel ist die Schaffung von attraktiven und bedürfnisgerechten Trails, welche sicher & möglichst nachhaltig gebaut sind, die Bikenden lenken und mittels "State-of-the-Art" Trail-Design optimalen Fahrspass ermöglichen.
  • Infrasturuktur-Typen sind:

Los 1) Eine naturnah gebaute Mountainbike-Strecke (Flow-/Style-Trail) in einfacher Schwierigkeit (blau), ⌀-Trail-Breite: 1.25m

Los 2) Zwei naturnah gebaute Mountainbike Strecken (1 x Tech-Trail und 1x Tech-/Style-Trail), beide in mittlerer Schwierigkeit (rot), ⌀-Trail-Breite: 1.1m

  • Als Bauwerke sind vorgesehen: Der Trail selbst, versch. Kunstbauten zu Gewässerquerungen, Holzstege, versch. Schikanen zur Geschwindigkeitsreduktion, Steinarmierungen zur nachhaltigen Sicherung der Wegoberfläche, optionale seitliche Trail-Features (Spiel-/Progressionselemente).
  • Zusätzlich fallen Ersatzmassnahmen an, welche aktuell noch in Abklärung & Planung sind. Diese werden ggf. zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt an den/die Anbieter vergeben. Hierfür werden nur die Regietarife von den Anbietern angefragt.
  • Alle weiteren Infos und techn. Angaben sind in den beigelegten Unterlagen (Auszug technischer Bericht und den Planbeilagen) zu entnehmen.

TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: PFAS-Free Sulfonated Poly(norbornene) Ionomeric Binders
description: A Cleaner, Tunable Alternative for Hydrogen Fuel Cells and Water Electrolyzers Hydrogen energy systems depend on a small but critical polymer layer inside each electrode, called an ionomeric binder, that shuttles protons, manages water and lets reactant gases reach the catalyst. The industry has long relied on perfluorosulfonic acid (PFSA) materials for this role, which contain PFAS (per? and polyfluoroalkyl substances) � �forever chemicals� � now under increasing regulatory pressure. Researchers at Los Alamos National Laboratory have developed a family of highly sulfonated poly(norbornene) ionomers that are entirely PFAS-free, deliver strong proton conductivity, do not poison precious-metal catalysts the way conventional aromatic alternatives do, and can be chemically tuned to keep electrodes dry under load. Together, these qualities position the material as a drop-in path forward for high-performance proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells and water electrolyzers in a tightening environmental landscape. How it Works PFAS-Free Sulfonated Poly(norbornene) Ionomeric Binders are a class of aliphatic sulfonated poly(norbornene) polymers designed specifically as electrode ionomers in proton-conducting devices. The polymer�s backbone is built from fused bicyclic norbornane units that lack the aromatic pi-electron systems found in conventional hydrocarbon ionomers. The absence of those electrons means the polymer does not strongly adsorb onto platinum catalyst surfaces, so catalytic activity is preserved. Sulfonic acid groups covalently attached onto this backbone supply the proton-conducting pathways, while the bulky bicyclic rings create extra free volume inside the polymer, allowing oxygen and hydrogen to diffuse more easily through the binder layer and reach the catalyst. By adjusting the ratio of sulfonated to non-sulfonated segments, the developers can dial in ionic activity and hydrophobicity to prevent electrode flooding, a persistent issue for PFAS-free ionomers when operated at high current density. Technology Description In a PEM fuel cell or water electrolyzer, the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) is the heart of the device, and the electrode ionomer inside it must simultaneously conduct protons, transport water, allow reactant gases to reach catalyst particles and bind mechanically to both the membrane and the catalyst layer. PFSA materials such as Nafion meet these requirements but carry the environmental burden associated with perfluorinated chemistries. Hydrocarbon-based sulfonated polymers offer a cleaner, lower-cost route, yet their phenyl-rich backbones tend to adsorb onto platinum and reduce catalytic activity, their gas permeability is typically low and the high sulfonic acid content needed for conductivity drives down hydrophobicity, leading to flooding under realistic operating conditions. PFAS-Free Sulfonated Poly(norbornene) Ionomeric Binders target each of these failure modes simultaneously by replacing the phenyl-heavy architecture with a sulfonated poly(norbornene) platform. Advantages Contains no PFAS, helping device makers stay ahead of tightening regulations on perfluorinated chemicals Maintains catalyst activity by avoiding the platinum-adsorbing phenyl groups common in other hydrocarbon ionomers Allows higher gas permeability for improved reactant transport at the electrode Offers tunable hydrophobicity to keep electrodes from flooding during demanding operation Built on a polymer platform with demonstrated thermal stability and mechanical durability Synthesized from lower-cost, structurally tunable starting materials compared with perfluorinated chemistries Market Applications Hydrogen Energy (PEM fuel cells, water electrolyzers, reversible fuel cells) Transportation (fuel cell vehicles, heavy-duty trucking, maritime auxiliary power) Stationary Power and Backup (data centers, telecom, distributed generation) Industrial Gas and Chemicals (hydrogen production for refining, ammonia, steel) Aerospace and Defense (unmanned systems, portable power packs) TRL 4 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-25232 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: True Silicone DLP Printing Platform
description: The True Silicone DLP Printing Platform from Los Alamos National Laboratory allows for more geometries in producing genuine silicone parts, gaskets, lattices, prosthetic components or microfluidic devices on an off-the-shelf desktop printer typically required by specialty extrusion equipment. The result is a material whose polymer backbone is built entirely of silicon-oxygen bonds rather than the carbon-based linkages that quietly compromise so-called silicones on the market today. The True Silicone DLP Printing Platform unlocks that capability through a precursor resin and a paired printing workflow that together deliver real silicone parts free of metal catalyst residues, with tunable porosity, geometric complexity and the aging stability that demanding applications require. How it Works The platform begins with a printable resin that blends a polymerizable scaffold with a curable siloxane component, along with a photoinitiator and a small amount of a light-absorbing dye to control polymerization depth. A standard DLP printer cures the acrylic scaffold layer by layer to lock the geometry in place, after which the part is heated so the siloxane oligomers crosslink into a continuous silicone network alongside the scaffold. A wash in ethanol, water or ammonium hydroxide then dissolves the sacrificial scaffold, leaving behind a pure silicone object whose polymer backbone consists solely of silicon�oxygen bonds and retains a porous structure where the sacrificial scaffold was removed. Technology Description At its core, the True Silicone DLP Printing Platform relies on a printable resin that combines two chemistries chosen to work in tandem: an acrylic component that polymerizes quickly under light to hold the printed geometry, and a silicone component that cures more slowly into the final material. During printing, these two phases remain mixed but separate into interwoven networks, an arrangement that lets the silicone retain the intended shape once the acrylic is later removed. A small amount of light-absorbing dye keeps polymerization confined to the intended pattern, and the resin is engineered to flow and cure reliably on standard DLP hardware. After printing, the part is gently heated to complete formation of the silicone network, then soaked in an alcohol or water-based wash, sometimes assisted by UV light or a mild base, to dissolve away the sacrificial acrylic scaffold. What remains is a silicone object whose polymer backbone is built entirely from silicon-oxygen bonds, with mechanical properties and a controllably porous structure whose open pores can be accessed after printing to imbue the silicone with new functionalities, for example by infusing conductive or otherwise active materials. The overall workflow is compatible with inexpensive commodity printers and lends itself to scaling through emerging light-based manufacturing techniques, while the same scaffold-and-wash strategy offers a template for printing other materials that have historically been difficult to fabricate by photopolymer methods. Advantages Produces true silicone with a continuous silicon-oxygen backbone, avoiding the aging and chemical-compatibility weaknesses of pseudo-silicone alternatives Runs on widely available, low-cost DLP printers rather than specialized direct-ink-write equipment Cures whole layers at once, delivering meaningfully higher throughput than extrusion-based silicone printing Yields parts free of residual metal catalysts, simplifying regulatory and biocompatibility pathways Allows tunable mechanical properties and porosity through resin ratios and porogenic solvent choice Extensible in principle to other material systems that currently resist photopolymer printing through the same sacrificial-scaffold approach Market Applications Medical and Consumer Health (prosthetics, wearable devices, soft implants) Sensing (stretchable circuits, soft robotics components) Microfluidics (lab-on-chip components, custom flow cells) Aerospace and Defense (cushioning foams, vibration-isolation components, sealing parts) Optics and Photonics (soft lenses, light-guiding elements) Consumer and Household Goods (kitchenware, mattresses, apparel components) Development Status: TRL 4 U.S. Patent No. 11,939,415 LA-UR-26-24892 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. description: On September 29, 2026, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Technology Acquisitions Center (TAC) in support of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), National Radiation Oncology Program, awarded a Firm Fixed Price contract to Radformation, Inc., 261 Madison Avenue New York, NY 10016, for an Enterprise-wide Radiotherapy Technical Quality Assurance (QA) System and Repository. The contract will provide a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) online, vendor-agnostic, enterprise-wide Software as a Service (SaaS) Radiotherapy Quality Assurance (QA) solution that standardizes, automates, and centralizes treatment delivery device QA data acquisition, analysis, and reporting across all VA Radiation Oncology Centers. The solution will streamline quality monitoring of linear accelerators (linacs) and other radiation treatment devices, including, but not limited to, brachytherapy and other non-linac teletherapy systems; imaging systems, including diagnostic systems such as computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) devices, as well as on-board imaging and other radiotherapy positioning verification and monitoring systems; and QA devices across diverse vendors. The solution shall comply with the applicable requirements of the American Association of Physicists in Medicine (AAPM) Task Group (TG)-142, TG-51, TG-198, as well as Medical Physics Practice Guidelines (MPPG) and Protocols. The period of performance shall consist of a 12-month base period, with four 12-month option periods.

title: Prestations d’ingénieur pour l’assainissement, le réaménagement et l’extension de la Stiegstrasse et du Stiegweg
description:
Le présent appel d’offres porte sur les prestations d’ingénierie relatives aux phases SIA 32 (Projet d’ouvrage) à 53 (Mise en service, clôture) pour la planification et la réalisation des infrastructures routières, des réseaux souterrains et des ouvrages de gestion des eaux dans le secteur du Sonnenberg.

Le projet comprend l’assainissement de la Stiegstrasse, la construction du nouveau Stiegweg ainsi que le renouvellement et l’extension des infrastructures de réseaux. Les principaux défis consistent en la réalisation de franchissements sans tranchée de la Sihltalstrasse et de la ligne SZU au moyen de microtunnelage et de forages par fonçage, la construction des puits nécessaires à ces travaux, ainsi que la coordination des différentes mesures relatives aux réseaux souterrains et aux canalisations. En outre, l’ensemble des procédures d’autorisation et d’approbation requises auprès des autorités compétentes et des propriétaires des réseaux devra être assuré.

Étendue des travaux :

  • Assainissement de la Stiegstrasse : env. 920 m
  • Construction du nouveau Stiegweg : env. 65 m
  • Construction d’une nouvelle conduite d’eaux pluviales : env. 800 m, y compris microtunnelage
  • Remplacement d’une conduite d’eau potable : env. 120 m, y compris forage par fonçage
  • Remplacement d’une conduite d’eaux mixtes : env. 120 m
  • Aménagements paysagers et espaces verts dans le périmètre du projet

title: Trøastrømmen Fv. 6466
description: 1 Arbeidenes art og omfang Langs Fv. 6466 (Dyrøyveien) på Trøa i Frøya kommune ligger Trøastrømmen bru (FV6466 K S1D1 m5929). Vegen over Trøastrømmen bru har en ÅDT på 675 med andel lange kjøretøy på 12%. Fartsgrense på stedet er 50 km/t. Dagens Trøastrømmen bru er bygget i 1960 og har følgende spesifikasjoner: • Spennvidde på ca.11,9m og total brulengde ca. 12,7m. Kjørebredden er på 3,75 m og total brubredde er 5,05 m. • Trøastrømmen bru er klassifisert for Bk 10/60, veggruppe A etter forsterkning av bjelker i 1999. • Landkar akse 1 er støpt betong, antatt uarmert. Fundamentering på fjæresteiner. Landkar akse 2 av murt naturstein, og fundamentert direkte på berg. • Vingemurer av murt naturstein. • Hovedbæring består av to stk HEA60 stålbjelker, fritt opplagt. • Brudekke av armert betong. • Brurekkverk av stål, byttet i 2020. • Brua har lengdefall 1:20 og tverrfall 1:25 Kappestøp av betong vil bli utført på begge landkar og tilhørende vingemurer i 2026 eller tidlig 2027. Se vedlegg av prosjekteringstegninger av kappestøp og fravik for bruk av landkar Brudekket har omfattende armeringskorrosjon og store skader, i tillegg til en del korrosjon på hovedbjelker. Trøndelag fylkeskommune anser derfor fullstendig bytte av bruoverbygning med rekkverk som nødvendig. Kontraktsarbeidet består av prosjektering og bygging av ny valgfri bruoverbygning til Trøastrømmen bru. Den nye konstruksjonen skal være tilpasset eksisterende landkar og ha føringsbredden og avstand mellom rekkverk på minst 5,0 m. Maks vekt av ny bruoverbygning kan ikke overstige 60 tonn. Grunnet mye trafikk og ingen omkjøringsmuligheter for nødetater og beboere, kan ikke Trøastrømmen være trafikkstengt i lengere periode enn en helg med ønsket stengetid så kort som mulig. Under stengeperioden skal det være etablert parkeringsplass til nødetater og beboere. Entreprenør står ansvarlig for å etablere/anskaffe en midlertidig parkering og nødvendig gangbru slik at det skal være mulig å krysse Trøastrømmen til fots. Prosjektet skal gjennomføres modellbasert, og modellinformasjon skal leveres i Trimble Connect-rom etablert av byggherre. I tillegg skal prosjektet suppleres med all nødvendig tegning der dette kreves for myndighetsbehandling og godkjenning (herunder kontroll og godkjenning fra Vegdirektoratet), samt med tegninger som ivaretar krav til drift og vedlikehold. Nærmere beskrivelse av omfang, funksjoner og krav er gitt konkurransegrunnlagets kapittel D. Krav til BIM Byggherren har lagt ved egen BIM-manual og matrise for egenskapsdatasett som entreprenøren med sine konsulenter forplikter å bruke i prosjektet, prosjekterende konsulent utarbeider fagspesifikke BIM-vedlegg etter eget behov. Byggherren oppretter prosjektrom i Trimble Connect hvor alt av modeller og tegninger skal leveres løpende gjennom hele prosjektet. Dette er primær plattform for all koordinering av modell og tegning.

title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Forschungsprojekt - DZSF - Mobilitätskettenanalyse - Wie Verkehrsdaten den ländlichen Schienenverkehr stärken können
description: Durch das Projekt sollen Mobilitätsketten im ländlichen Raum mittels einer Methodentriangulation analysiert und dabei insbesondere die Rolle des Schienenpersonenverkehrs (SPV) untersucht werden. Ein Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem Vergleich und der Verknüpfung von objektiven Verkehrsdaten mit subjektiven Angaben zur Nutzung und Wahrnehmung der verschiedenen Verkehrsmittel. Neben dem Sammeln und Erheben von Daten in ausgewählten Fokusregionen, dienen ergänzende, experimentelle Studien dazu, kausale Aussagen über die Wirksamkeit von Maßnahmen zur Förderung des Nutzens nachhaltiger Mobilitätsketten im ländlichen Raum anstellen zu können.

title: Netherlands – Construction work – RWK Programma
description: Brabant Water staat aan de vooravond van een omvangrijk meerjarig programma gericht op het toekomstbestendig maken van het reinwaterkelderareaal (verder: RWK Programma). Aanleiding voor dit programma zijn onder meer eerdere incidenten met verontreinigingen, de toenemende leeftijd en diversiteit van het RWK‑areaal en aangescherpte eisen ten aanzien van kwaliteit, veiligheid en beveiliging van de drinkwatervoorziening. Uit inventarisaties is gebleken dat een deel van de reinwaterkelders niet langer voldoet, waardoor ingrijpen noodzakelijk is om de betrouwbaarheid en continuïteit van de watervoorziening op de lange termijn te borgen. Om de leveringszekerheid nu en in de toekomst te waarborgen voert de afdeling productie van Brabant Water één openbare aanbesteding verdeeld in twee percelen gericht op het contracteren van langjarige samenwerkingspartners voor het ontwerp en de realisatie van RWK projecten uit. Het programma heeft tot doel het reinwaterkelderareaal toekomstbestendig te maken en daarmee de betrouwbaarheid, kwaliteit en continuïteit van de drinkwatervoorziening voor de komende decennia te borgen. Vanuit de marktconsultatie is het RWK Programma opgezet met een duidelijk programmatische aanpak, continuïteit in opdrachtverlening en ruimte voor samenwerking en kennisontwikkeling. Voor meer inhoudelijke informatie verwijzen wij naar de aanvraag van Perceel 1 "Nieuwbouw" en Perceel 2 "Voorbouw en Maatwerk"

Utilities Privatization (UP) is defined as the transfer of ownership and responsibility to a municipal, private, regional, district, or cooperative utility company or other entity, for the operations, maintenance, repair, future upgrades, and future utility systems replacements. The conveyance may consist of all right, title, and interest of the United States in the utility system. UP will be accomplished in accordance with 10 U.S.C. �2688 � Utility Systems: Conveyance Authority. As a result of this solicitation, the Contractor(s) will be selected to assume ownership of the Water utility system. The new owner(s) shall operate and maintain the system and provide utility services to the Government. Any resulting contract, if awarded, will require the Contractor to furnish all facilities, labor, materials, tools, and equipment necessary to own, maintain, and operate the utility system. All responsibility for maintaining reliable service, including such items as environmental compliance, maintenance costs, major system renovations, construction, equipment, manpower, and overhead costs shall become the utility system owner�s responsibility. The Contractor shall manage the maintenance, repairs, replacement, etc., of the system to ensure continuous, adequate, and dependable service for each Government or tenant connection within the service area. The Contractor shall be responsible for funding all capital investments required to acquire, maintain, and operate the utility system in a safe, reliable condition and to meet the requirements listed in the contract. Real property interests will be conveyed in the form of a Right to Access or an Easement as a reference to the resultant contract. description: Dem LZN obliegt die Beschaffung von Waren und Dienstleistungen für die unmittelbare niedersächsische Landesverwaltung (vgl. § 2 der Betriebsanweisung des LZN). Mit Zustimmung seiner Aufsichtsbehörde kann das LZN weitere Aufgaben für öffentlich-rechtliche Bedarfsträger innerhalb und außerhalb der niedersächsischen Landesverwaltung sowie für privatrechtliche Gesellschaften in vollständiger Eigentümerschaft der öffentlichen Hand übernehmen (vgl. § 3 Betriebsanweisung). In dieser Zuständigkeit umfasst der Auftrag den Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung mit einem Unternehmen (§ 21 VgV) über die Lieferung von Wollunterwäsche für die Kooperationspartner der norddeutschen Küstenländer der Polizei und Justiz, der Landesforsten und Ordnungsämtern innerhalb von Deutschland und sonstige Behörden (gemäß Anlage) mit einer Preisbindung von 24 Monaten sowie optional zwei einseitige Vertragsverlängerungen zu jeweils höchstens 12 Monaten mit einem Unternehmen. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind der Leistungsbeschreibung -Technischer Teil (Teil B) inkl. Angebotsvordruck zu entnehmen. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind den technischen Lieferbedingungen und dem Angebotsvordruck zu entnehmen.

buyer: Aufbau- und Entwicklungsgesellschaft Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler mbH
title: Germany – Construction work – 1H0007, Neubau Feuerwehr Ahrweiler - Los 070 Gebäudeautomation
description: Neubau der Feuerwehr Ahrweiler: Das heutige Gebäude der Freiwilligen Feuerwehr Ahrweiler an der Ramersbacher Straße gegenüber des Ahrtores wurde durch die Flut im Jahr 2021 stark beschädigt. Der verbleibende Torso ist nicht mehr sanierungsfähig, sodass an anderer Stelle ein Ersatzneubau mit 12 Stellplätzen realisiert werden soll. Die neue Lage südlich der Ahr befindet sich in Sichtweite des heutigen Feuerwehrgebäudes. Durch die Umlegung des Feuerwehrgebäudes soll in Zukunft die Erreichbarkeit aller Gebiete auch bei extremen Hochwasser durch die Feuerwehr sichergestellt werden. Im Rahmen von Los 070 wird die Gebäudeautomation ausgeschrieben. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst die Lieferung, Montage und Inbetriebnahme aller Mess-, Steuer- und Regeltechnikkomponenten einschließlich Feldgeräten, Automationsstationen, Netzwerktechnik und Schaltschränken. Zudem sind die vollständige Verkabelung, die Einrichtung der Gebäudeleittechnik, die Programmierung, Prüfungen, Dokumentation sowie die Einweisung des Bedienpersonals auszuführen. Alle Arbeiten erfolgen gemäß VOB/C und den geltenden Normen und Richtlinien, um einen sicheren und zuverlässigen Betrieb der neuen Feuerwache sicherzustellen.

title: Finland – Construction work – SR-urakka, Uudisrakennus, Helsinki, Hermanni, Heka Hermanninranta Albumikatu 3
description: Hankinnan kohteena on asuinkerrostalojen rakentaminen Helsingin Hermanninrantaan SR-urakkana sisältäen kokonaissuunnittelun (mm. ark, rak, lvias, energia, pohjarakennus, elinkaari, akustiikka) ja rakennusteknisten töiden lisäksi kaikki LVIAS- ja pihatyöt. Kokonaisurakkaan lukeutuvat: - Tontit 21685/2 ja 21685/3 (yhdistetään mahdollisesti myöhemmin) Heka Hermanninranta Albumikatu 3 Hankkeen erityispiirteitä: - Kohde koostuu kahdesta erillisestä kerrostalosta ja piha-alueesta, jotka muodostavat puolet korttelikokonaisuudesta. - Kohde voidaan toteuttaa joko puu- tai betonirunkoisena. Betonirunko edellyttää poikkeamispäätöksen hakemista, josta urakoitsija vastaa. - Asuntoala n. 11 040 asm2 ja liiketilan ala n. 55 htm2 lukeutuvat tarjouspyyntöön hankittavaan määrään. - Urakoitsija vastaa kaikesta suunnittelusta. Suunnittelu voidaan aloittaa esisopimuksen allekirjoituksen jälkeen. Rakennustyön arvioitu alkamisajankohta on 04/2028 ja työt tulee aloittaa viimeistään 06/2028. Hankintaa ei jaeta osiin, sillä usean toimittajan malli tuottaisi epätarkoituksenmukaisen sopimuskokonaisuudenaikataulunhallinnan sekä töiden yhteensovittamisen kannalta. Hankinnan kohde on tarkemmin kuvattu tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevissa kaupallisissa ja teknisissä asiakirjoissa. Liiteasiakirjat löytyvät julkaisun Tarjouspalvelu-sivuilta kohdassa "Liitteet ja linkit" ilmoitetusta linkistä.

title: France – Public road transport services – DELEGATION DE SERVICE PUBLIC RELATIVE A LA GESTION ET L’EXPLOITATIONDES SERVICES DE MOBILITE ET DE TRANSPORT DE VOYAGEURS SUR LETERRITOIRE DE CHATEAUROUX METROPOLE
description: La consultation a pour objet de déléguer la gestion et l’exploitation des services de mobilité et de transport de voyageurs sur le ressort territorial de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole (Réseau Horizon) Châteauroux Métropole, autorité Organisatrice de la mobilité est autorité délégante. Les missions déléguées sont les suivantes: Offre de base : Exploitation et gestion des services de mobilité et de transports publics de personnes et à l’échelle du territoire communautaire selon les principes définis à l’article 5.1 du document programme. Les candidats devront obligatoirement répondre à l’offre de base et à l'option obligatoire.• Option obligatoire :Option N°1 : Exploitation et gestion d’un service de location de vélos L’option est décrite à l’article 5.2 du document programme. L’Autorité Délégante précisera, avant la remise de l'offre finale si l'option est levée. Le Délégataire assurera la gestion de ces services pour une durée de six (6) ans, à compter du 01/01/2028 et jusqu’au 31/12/2033 dans le cadre d’une délégation de service public (DSP) au sein du périmètre contractuel. Lieu d’exécution : Territoire de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole(département de l’Indre). L’estimation de la valeur du contrat de concession est de 45 millions d’euros HT valeur décembre 2026 sur la durée du contrat. Les missions attendues sont l'organisation, la production et la commercialisation des services, ainsi que la réalisation de l'offre de transport et la maintenance des véhicules et outils de production.Le délégataire assurera en outre la gestion de la relation avec les usagers des transports scolaires qui sont assurés par le biais de marchés publics en cours. La future DSP intègre la gestion et l'exploitation des services de transport suivants sur l’ensemble du périmètre de l’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole : • Le réseau de transport en commun « Horizon » composé aujourd’hui de 12 lignes régulières, • Le service de transport adapté à la demande, « Handibus », à destination des personnes à mobilité réduite sur le périmètre de CM .Pour cette gestion déléguée, la collectivité met à la disposition du délégataire : • Un dépôt de bus réceptionné en 2021 avec une capacité de stationnement de 80 véhicules, équipé de bureaux, d’un atelier de maintenance, de stations de lavage et de carburant et d’équipements de recharge de véhicule électrique; • 31 autobus standard, 5 autobus articulé, 2 midibus. Ces véhicules sont équipés d’équipements de suivi par système SAEIV et cellules de comptage voyageurs. Plusieurs véhicules standard et articulés électriques ont également été commandés. • 2 midibus accessibles et équipés pour accueillir des PMR • Un Site Internet https://www.bushorizon.com/ La présente concession est passée sur le fondement du règlement 1370/2007 et de la directive 2014/23/CEE. La directive 2014/25/UE citée dans le présent avis concerne les marchés des secteurs spéciaux est non les concessions , elle ne s'applique pas à la présente consultation.

description:
Les CFF recherchent un fournisseur capable de livrer environ 9 millions de litres de diesel par camion-citerne à quelque 70 stations-service ferroviaires réparties dans toute la Suisse. Un carburant diesel semi-renouvelable (actuellement du diesel B0 HVO avec mélange 25% conforme à la norme SN EN 590) est prévu pour environ 1000 véhicules sur rails à moteur diesel et autres applications. Dans le cadre de leur stratégie de développement durable, les CFF souhaitent pouvoir s’approvisionner en produits diesel à forte part d’énergies renouvelables, tels que le R32, le HVO93 ou le HVO100. Les prérequis sont l’aptitude technique, la disponibilité, le respect des exigences de durabilité et des surcoûts économiquement acceptables. Le respect du concept de pénurie d’électricité constitue une exigence logistique supplémentaire. 

Le marché porte également sur la livraison annuelle d’environ 3 millions de litres d’huile de chauffage à environ 180 adresses. Pour l’huile de chauffage, un système de télésurveillance devra être mis en place dans les douze mois suivant la signature du contrat. Le soumissionnaire surveille les stocks et émet une recommandation de commande en cas de non-respect des stocks minimaux définis.

title: R799--East Orange EUL Development Opportunity Sources Sought COR: Sharon Sirotnak
description: East Orange, NJ EUL Request for Expressions of Interest DRAFT PRE-DECISIONAL INTERNAL VA USE ONLY 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY VA New Jersey Healthcare System (VANJHCS) within Veterans Integrated Service Network 2 (VISN 2) East Orange, NJ VA Medical Center (VAMC) located within East Orange, NJ Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the asset described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing administrative and/or educational purposes, or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., technical skills / job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). Parking is limited on the campus and if redevelopment would result in significantly increased demand for parking, parking must be included within the footprint. For purposes of this effort, the Developer would be a non-VA entity who has the qualifications outlined in Section V of this Notice. The opportunity would involve a Developer entering into an EUL with VA and financing, renovating/constructing, operating, and maintaining the agreed upon use of the asset. VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose an asset at the East Orange VAMC Campus under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Additional information on the VA s EUL program may be obtained at: http://www.va.gov/assetmanagement/. Development Scope The intent of this Notice is to determine if there are experienced developers, including SDVOSB or VOSB developers, that can develop the subject Campus asset in accordance with VA s EUL authority. The Developer would undertake all necessary investigation activities to produce development with the underutilized asset at the East Orange Campus. The asset that may be redeveloped by the Developer includes Building 11 (Note: The building is currently listed on the National Register of Historic Places). Please see Attachment A for a map of the Campus and Attachment B for asset information and photos. East Orange VA Medical Center Background The East Orange VA Medical Center located at 385 Tremont Avenue, East Orange, NJ 07018-1023 includes ~34 acres situated on a knoll at South Center Street and Tremont Avenue, 228 feet above sea level. The campus overlooks a residential area with views of the Manhattan skyline on the horizon. The grounds are in four municipalities: Orange, East Orange, South Orange, and Newark. The site formerly belonged to the Bamberger estate, which was endowed originally to Princeton University and in turn, sold to a private owner and then purchased by the government. Recognizing the need for a medical facility to serve Veterans in metropolitan areas, Congress approved and funded the facility in 1943. The VAMC opened in July 1952. The hospital provides primary care and specialty health services, including homeless Veteran care, mental health care, skin care (dermatology), dental care, digestive care (gastroenterology), cardiology, eye health and vision care (ophthalmology and optometry), palliative and hospice care, returning service member care, Veteran readiness and employment programs, and more. Sources Sought Response Requirements VA is seeking qualified developers who have a proven company track record of: Developing projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated asset. Financial wherewithal required to successfully develop the proposed use(s) with associated amenities (if applicable); and, Securing public and private financing for projects comparable to the proposed use(s) for the designated asset. For SDVOSB/VOSB developers, VA is seeking to confirm the Respondent s ability to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Responses should be submitted on official letterhead, must include a point of contact and the signature of at least one organization officer. Responses must address the following elements in sufficient detail to highlight the Respondent s ability to undertake the development scope as set forth in this Sources Sought Notice. Responses must not exceed 15 pages, single spaced with a minimum 12-point font. Response content should consist of the following: Business Information Please provide the following for your company: Company Name Address Point of Contact Phone Number E-mail Address Web Page URL SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Based on the NAICS Code i

description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking concerns having the ability for providing Residential Reentry Center (RRC) services (in-house RRC beds) and Home Confinement services (home confinement placements) for male and female Federal offenders held under the authority of United States Statutes Residential Reentry Center Services located within Sacramento County and other border Counties of San Jaquin, Sutter, Yolo, Solano, Placer, El Dorado, and Amador. Home Confinement within 150 miles of the RRC Facility. Both the RRC services for in-house RRC beds and the Home Confinement services for home confinement placements shall be in accordance with the Federal Bureau of Prisons Statement of Work (SOW) entitled, �Residential Reentry Center, March 2022�. Home Confinement services (for home confinement placements) are specifically defined in chapter 10, programs, of the SOW. Additional requirements for these services are referenced throughout the SOW as well. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price/IDIQ contract for services with a one-year base period, and four one-year options periods. The RRC In-House requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 16 beds in which 14 beds will be designated for males and 2 beds designated for females and an estimated maximum 40 bed facility in which 34 beds will be designated for males and 6 beds designated for females. The Home Confinement requirement will consist of a guaranteed minimum 8 placements and an estimated maximum 20 placements to include both male and female. It is the intent of the Government to award both line items (RRC in-house beds and home confinement placements) to a single provider, as these services are interconnected and rely upon each other to ensure adequate programming and case management of offenders. The Government reserves the right to potentially make an award which is deemed to be in the best interest of the Government. The closing date of 15BRRC26R00000019 is January 08, 2027 at 2:00pm EST. All responsible sources may submit a proposal which will be considered by this agency. No collect calls will be accepted. No telephone request or written requests for the solicitation will be accepted.

title: Germany – Facade work – Geb. 3704 Neubau Digital Innovation Campus (1. BA) - VE306 - Fassadenarbeiten
description: Im Zuge der Neubaumaßnahme der Leibniz Universität Hannover wird der erste Bauabschnitt des Institutsgebäudes 3 704 "D igital Innovation Campus" mit einer BGF von ca . 4 .600 m 2 errichtet. Das Gebäude soll zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt um einen zweiten Bauabschnitt ( v on ca. 2 .300 m2 BGF) erweitert werden. Der Neubau vervollständigt den vorhandenen Block aus bestehenden Universitätsgebäuden nach Nordosten hin. Der Eingang ist zum Blockinnenbereich nach Süden zum bestehenden Campus hin orientiert. Geplant ist ein kompakter, annähernd quadratischer Baukörper mit den Abmessungen 33 x 32,50m im Grundriss und einem Untergeschoss über die gesamte Fläche sowie drei Obergeschossen. Im ersten Obergeschoss befindet sich nach Osten orientiert ein offener Innenhof . D ie Geschosshöhen betragen 4,26m im Erdgeschoss und 3,50m in den Obergeschossen. Es handelt sich um ein Institutsgebäude mit überwiegend Büronutzung in den Obergeschossen und Unterrichtsbereichen mit Hörsaal im Erdgeschoss.

title: A Study on Vessel Design Challenge
description: U.S. Maritime Administration (MARAD) A Study on Vessel Design Challenge RFP No. 693JF726R000016 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP): The Maritime Administration�s (MARAD) Maritime Environmental and Technical Assistance (META) program is issuing a request for proposals (RFP) for a Vessel Design Challenge (Challenge). This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. � 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America�s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. PROPOSAL CONTENT Proposed Vessel Design: Design proposals can include: Existing projects that would be redesigned, Forthcoming projects that are just beginning the design specification phase, and Designs that are theoretical or more experimental which aim to create a new approach or design. There are no restrictions on eligible vessels, however, given the mission of the Maritime Administration, vessels should be commercially useful and generally would not include small watercraft, recreational vessels, or fisheries vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team�s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only �lead� one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating �leads� will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. This Challenge intends to fund multiple design teams willing to undertake integrated design work to improve fuel efficiency and reduce vessel underwater radiated noise (URN) to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Individual awards depend on number of designs proposed for the package. Awards are intended to be for not less than $150k and likely not more than $450k. Project completion timeline is 12-18 months. Total funding available is up to $1.25 million. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: The META program (46 U.S.C. � 50307) is investigating the interconnections between broader fuel efficiency, reducing URN from vessels, and exploring potential co-benefits. It is the policy of the United States to revitalize and rebuild domestic maritime industries and workforce to promote national security and economic prosperity. Accomplishing this requires making United States-flagged and built vessels commercially competitive in international commerce, rebuilding America�s maritime manufacturing capabilities, and expanding and strengthening the recruitment, training, and retention of the relevant workforce. The most promising opportunities for optimizing fuel efficiency gains and achieving URN reductions are in the early ship design stage, using a systems approach. This requires intentional and integrated ship designs that prioritize fuel efficiency while simultaneously reducing URN. Advanced fluid dynamic modeling enables comparison among hull, engine, and propeller design and arrangement, providing valuable information to the industry about the return on investment (ROI) for various technology and design optimizations at the design phase. Individual technologies claim to provide efficiency and noise reduction benefits, but the additive cost-savings have not been quantified for applying technologies in series and demonstrating increased efficiencies across multiple areas. Recently published studies summarized the state of knowledge and availability of technologies that can be applied to vessels to improve energy efficiency while reducing vessel generated URN. Those reports crosswalk not only the interoperability of technologies and design elements, but the potential reductions, costs, and return on investment. The next phase is to demonstrate, through modeling, the benefits that can be realized through a systematic design approach integrating technologies with input from naval architects, shipyards, and technology suppliers on the efficacy of these approaches. By using this approach, Teams will begin at the drawing table to quantify the benefits of innovative technology integration into the design phase for application on new vessels. The Vessel Design Challenge is intended to facilitate the demonstration of novel vessel designs that meet or exceed international benchmarks for fuel efficiency and URN source levels. This Challenge is intended to fund multiple Design Teams willing to undertake this kind of integrated design work to create the next generation of U.S. vessels. Eligible designs include vessels operating in coastal or inland waterways as well as the Great Lakes. Ideal proposals will be for new design approaches or design modifications that couple hull-machinery-propulsion approaches to maximize fuel efficiency, URN reduction, and ROI. Technologies should be centered around performance and demonstrating the feasibility and economic achievability of these combined approaches and should be dictated by capacity needs set by industry requirements (tug capacity, crew capacity, operations support, range, TEU, cargo etc.). Designs should note specifically the technology readiness level and the commercial availability of any technologies used. Design Team: The approach to the Challenge will include a design team. Teams should include description of partnerships, collaborations, and/or processes that will ensure success of the proposal. Further, proposals should identify the Team�s capabilities, related experience, techniques, or unique combinations of these that are integral factors for achieving the Challenge objectives to include experience that supports ability to successfully manage and achieve project goals and objectives of similar type and scope. Development of an ideal team should represent the concept of a design-build approach and include: Naval architect(s) Marine Engineer(s) Shipyard(s) Owner/operator/buyer (can be more than one) Technology provider(s) (including fuel supplier, as needed) May include operator/charter party, BCO, logistics partners, port/city/public entity, private financing partner. Teams may submit one or more vessel designs to the Challenge. Funding amounts will be based on: the number of vessel designs proposed their technology innovation, or a combination thereof One or all proposed designs may be funded depending on proposals. There is no limit to number of teams an organization can participate in, however, an organization may only �lead� one team/proposal. No identical teams with rotating �leads� will be permitted. Preference will be given to proposals with team leads represented by U.S. companies, those with U.S. headquarters, and those operating under the U.S. flag Methods: Proposals must include a detailed description of the design and modeling approaches that will be used to meet the Design Challenge Parameters as noted below, including those for fuel burn estimates and URN source level as well as modeling for return on investment and similar economic estimates and valuations. Timeline: The proposed plan should include the expected timeline (not to exceed 18 months) inclusive of kick off meetings with MARAD, design and technology integration and assessment, interim progress report detailing vessel design and technology application progress, data collection and analysis, and final report deliverables. Budget: All proposals must include a compete, detailed, and justifiable budget with general line items for various design components and stages including fuel, URN, and ROI evaluation and calculations. Budgets should demonstrate market conditions or similar that support these budget estimates. Description of key personnel, qualifications, and expected level of effort should also be included. Proposals may also include any additional considerations, outreach, or analysis recommended to achieve the goals of the project. Design Challenge Parameters Design specifications: The objective is for designs to meet or exceed these specifications for fuel efficiency improvement and noise reduction. Recognizing that this is a demonstration of technical feasibility and economic achievability, if these design specifications are not achievable, alternative efficiency and noise improvements should be documented demonstrating the current limits of technologies. These specifications should be considered aspirational to test the limits of the possible within the bounds of the practical. Energy Efficiency: 30% efficiency improvement over a typical vessel design with conventional hull and machinery arrangements and fuels. description: Le marché porte sur l’étude et la construction en Entreprise Totale des parties d’ouvrages suivantes : 1. Nouvelle station de découplage (SDD) y compris les adaptations hydrauliques dans les stations de pompage (SPP), les conduites de liaison SPP et SDD et les conduites de rejet au lac entre le bâtiment SDD et la chambre de visite d’interface des conduites CCU/SDD. 2. Nouvelles conduites de liaison (terrestres) SDD-PDR jusqu’au poste de redistribution PDR, y compris la création d’un nouveau local de pompes dans l’actuel parking au sous-sol du bâtiment BS de l’EPFL. 3. L’Entreprise Totale interviendra de la phase « 32. Projet d’ouvrage » jusqu’à la phase « 53. Mise en service, achèvement ». L’élément déclencheur et l’objectif primordial du projet est la protection contre la prolifération des moules Quagga dans nos conduites et la sécurisation du réseau de refroidissement. De ce fait, le projet comprend les trois objectifs ci-dessous : 1. Protection totale des conduites du réseau de refroidissement contre la prolifération des moules Quagga, grâce au découplage hydraulique et à un nouveau réseau en boucle fermée. 2. Augmentation des capacités en refroidissement afin de subvenir aux besoins futurs dus aux nouveaux bâtiments et à l’augmentation de la demande des bâtiments existants. 3.
